\[
r_s = \frac{r\, (1 - k\, r^2)}{1 - k},
\qquad k = 0.15
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(r\): The distance of an output pixel from the image center, as a share of half the diagonal
- \(r_s\): The distance of the source position it reads, in the same unit
- \(k\): The strength, the size of the negative radial term

This is the barrel mapping with a negative coefficient. The source radius grows slower than the output radius toward the edges, so the outer part of the image is stretched outward and straight lines bow inward. The strength stops at 0.3, below one third, because the mapping folds back on itself when 3 k r^2 reaches 1 at the corners. Keep corners divides by 1 - k so that the corners stay. Each output pixel reads the source at the mapped position with bilinear interpolation, the inverse mapping of Gonzalez and Woods, so no holes appear.
